# App updates, ads and sponsors, remote switches

## Architecture invariants

- App updates (owner request 2026-10-20, [spec](docs/specs/2026-10-20-check-for-updates.md)): the drawer's Check for updates asks GitHub's releases API only when tapped; Settings → App updates → Update automatically (off by default) checks once a day on opening, downloads on Wi-Fi and installs when the app leaves the screen, never while a video plays. Downloads come only from GitHub hosts, must match GitHub's SHA-256 digest and be a newer version of this package before `update/AppUpdater.kt` hands them to `PackageInstaller` (`REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES`, allowed in `tools/report_apk.py` for this only). Preview builds update to newer builds of the same PR from the `preview` release; local builds only open GitHub. Interrupted updates (owner pick 2026-11-08, [spec](docs/specs/2026-11-08-retry-interrupted-updates.md)): the download lives in `cacheDir/app-update/` with `update.json` describing it, so it survives the app being closed, a broken one carries on with an HTTP `Range` request, an install Android never answered shows Install again when the app returns, and the APK is deleted once the new version opens. Smaller updates (owner pick 2026-11-08, [spec](docs/specs/2026-11-08-smaller-app-updates.md)): each release publishes patches from its last 15 releases (`tools/apk_patch.py`, listed in `update-info.json`'s `patches`), and each preview build one from the build it replaces; the app rebuilds the new APK from its installed one (`data/UpdatePatches.kt`), which must still match the release's SHA-256, and downloads the whole APK when anything about the patch fails. The release APK carries ARM libraries only (`abiFilters` in `app/build.gradle.kts`; debug and benchmark builds keep every ABI), so a device that can't run ARM apps gets `UpdateChannel.UnsupportedDevice`. Never add a project server or a store. Scale readiness (owner request 2026-10-30, [spec](docs/specs/2026-10-30-scale-readiness.md)): Settings → App updates → Tell me about new versions (on by default) makes the daily check read the latest release's `update-info.json` (download hosts, not the rate-limited API) and show a banner for a new version (at most once a week whatever the version, so daily releases never bring a daily banner, and not in the week after the app was installed or updated; Skip this version) or, below the newest `security:critical` release, a Security update dialog (no skip; after Not now daily for that fix's first 3 days, then weekly, and a newer fix starts again), never over a playing video; turning the setting off sends nothing and says that security updates go unannounced too; the release workflow writes that file and publishing requires it. The same check reads `remote-config/switches.json` (remote switches, switches only: reorder or drop built-in Google addresses, slow background translation, turn Skip ads, Skip sponsors or page-token captions off, show a built-in notice); never let it carry code, scripts, selectors or addresses. Menu → Report a problem shows the local problem log (`data/ProblemLog.kt`: step names, statuses, Google addresses; never video IDs, titles or text) and opens an email to `PROBLEM_REPORT_EMAIL` (dualsubreplay.help@gmail.com, the project's report inbox) or a prefilled GitHub issue in an in-app browser tab, which the person sends; nothing is uploaded by itself.

- Ads & sponsors (owner request 2026-10-25, [spec](docs/specs/2026-10-25-skip-ads-and-sponsors.md)): Settings → Ads & sponsors → Skip ads and Skip sponsors, both on by default. YouTube's ads still load; `WEB_AD_SKIP_SCRIPT` (`ui/AdSkipScripts.kt`) only mutes the page video and plays it at 4x while the player shows an ad, presses YouTube's own Skip and banner-close buttons (YouTube ignores a script's press of Skip, so the app also taps the shown Skip button with a real touch, only where `elementFromPoint` is that button, never the ad video), and gives the sound and speed back afterwards. Never block ad requests or edit YouTube's replies (the owner picked skipping over blocking). Sponsor parts come only from SponsorBlock (`data/SponsorSegments.kt`: `sponsor.ajay.app/api/skipSegments/<4 hex of the SHA-256 of the video ID>`, `sponsor` category only, in memory only; data CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, credited in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the licence screen) and are jumped over once when the video plays into them; a seek into one keeps it unless Always skip sponsors (off by default, owner request 2026-10-25) is on.
